items.title: Meta faces 'tobacco moment' in landmark child harm trial
items.summary: OAKLAND: Jury selection kicked off on Wednesday in a California courtroom where Instagram and Facebook owner Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial which experts describe as social media's big tobacco moment. Federal Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers and lawyers for both sides probed prospective jurors about their views of social media and Meta, asking if they personally had social media accounts, whether their kids use social media, and if they think social media is responsible for mental health, among other questions. Some said they believed that social media plays a role in mental health, with one person comparing the serotonin boost that some people feel from "doomscrolling" to using cocaine.

items.title: Malaysia's multi-billion BESS race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Renewable energy (RE) construction flows in Malaysia are expected to pick up in the coming months, with battery energy storage systems (BESS) being the next phase of growth. Malaysia is mandating BESS for major solar power projects nationwide to ensure grid stability. "A data centre could combine grid plus solar plus BESS plus conventional backup.

items.title: Ignoring the noise when investing
items.summary: Social media, market commentators and investment websites generate a continuous stream of news, opinions, predictions and price movements. For the long-term investor, however, much of this information is simply noise. Successful investing requires the discipline to distinguish temporary market fluctuations from genuine changes in a company's underlying fundamentals.

items.title: Boeing ordered to pay US$29mil to family of 737 MAX crash victim
items.summary: NEW YORK: A Chicago jury awarded US$29 million in damages to the family of an Irish-born United Nations employee who died in a 2019 Boeing 737 MAX crash, a US court spokesman said Wednesday. The civil suit was brought against Boeing by Naoise Connolly Ryan, widow of Michael "Mick" Ryan, an engineer with the UN World Food Programme who was one of the victims in the Ethiopian Airlines crash that killed all 157 people on board. The case is one of the final remaining civil suits pending against Boeing following the pair of deadly MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019 that together claimed 346 lives.

items.title: Credible missile threat prompted secret Trump aircraft switch
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A threat that Air Force One could be targeted by a shoulder-fired missile prompted the Secret Service to secretly move President Donald Trump onto a smaller government jet during a trip to Turkiye last month, a person briefed on the matter said on Wednesday. The threat emerged on the final day of Trump's visit to Ankara for the Nato summit amid heightened tensions with Iran, the source said. The Secret Service deemed the threat to be credible and imminent, prompting an extraordinary operation to conceal the US president's movements.

items.title: Tabung Haji tightens fund oversight, investment monitoring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji is reviewing its framework in overseeing and monitoring its funds and investment management to strengthen its governance according to the Tabung Haji Act 1995. The move was significant given that the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) had recommended reforms to Tabung Haji's governance and investment framework. The RCI also proposed that Tabung Haji's investment function be managed through a dedicated department, known as Dana Haji, which would remain within the fund, but registered or licensed by the Securities Commission.

items.title: Trump authorises cyber operations targeting transnational crime groups
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump signed a memo on Wednesday that the White House said was aimed at empowering federal law enforcement to use cyber tools against transnational criminal organisations that operate in foreign jurisdictions to attack Americans. Trump signed the national security presidential memorandum directing his administration to "leverage the capability and innovation of the private sector to help conduct these cyber operations under the direction, control, and authority of the US Government," the White House said. The White House, in a fact sheet about the memo, cited ransomware attacks, financial frauds and other crimes run by foreign-based organised criminal organizations.

items.title: Expert: 'Kootu' scheme contributors not automatically offenders
items.summary: Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM) School of Law senior lecturer Dr Muhammad Hafiz Badarulzaman said the Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act 1971 primarily targeted those who operated or promoted kootu funds as a business. He said businesses set up to promote kootu funds could not be registered under the Registration of Businesses Act 1956. He said traditional kootu arrangements without profit, interest or membership fees were not prohibited under the Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act 1971.

items.title: Wong Chen exit exposes deeper challenge for PKR, say analysts [WATCH]
items.summary: International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) political analyst Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said PKR must now re-examine its identity and future direction following Wong's departure to Parti Bersama Malaysia. "For PKR, this means they are losing their reformist faction. Universiti Malaya sociopolitical analyst Professor Datuk Dr Awang Azman Awang Pawi said Wong's departure hurt PKR "symbolically more than numerically" for now.

items.title: When neutrality pays: How Malaysia is navigating the global fuel crisis
items.summary: Almost 40 per cent of Malaysia’s crude oil imports pass through the waterway, making any prolonged disruption a significant concern for the country’s energy security. Malaysia, a net importer of crude oil, produces about 350,000 barrels of oil a day but consumes about 700,000 barrels, according to the Finance Ministry. Malaysia also subsidises fuel for domestic consumption, keeping pump prices below those in some major oil-producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

items.title: MAHA 2026 to focus on smart farming and automation
items.summary: SERDANG: Smart farming, automation and agricultural technology will take centre stage at MAHA 2026 as Malaysia steps up efforts to strengthen food security and boost productivity across the agri-food sector. Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak said this year's exhibition would place greater emphasis on technology, innovation, processing and marketing, rather than just agricultural production. "It must also encompass technology, innovation, processing and marketing," he said during a media briefing on MAHA 2026, here, yesterday.

items.title: Fadhlina: Teach children to speak up, disagree respectfully
items.summary: CHILDREN should not only be taught to be well-behaved, but also to have the confidence to speak up, think critically and disagree respectfully, said Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek. She said character education was needed to train them to articulate their views, challenge opposing opinions and defend their positions without compromising courtesy. "Character education is not just about teaching children to be good.

items.title: Trump sued over paid early access to market-moving Truth Social posts
items.summary: NEW YORK: Donald Trump was sued on Wednesday by two media entities seeking to shut down a new service that sells paid access to the US president's posts, including some that can move markets, on his Truth Social platform. The complaint filed in Manhattan federal court by the Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation challenges Truth API, a feed offered by Trump Media & Technology Group that charges up to US$100,000 a month for early access to 10 high-profile Truth Social accounts, including Trump's own. Other White House officials are also defendants but Trump Media is not.

items.title: Govt to boost airport security, border cooperation
items.summary: COMPREHENSIVE plan to improve airport security will be tabled at the cabinet meeting next week. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said yesterday the plan would cover agency coordination, personnel training, infrastructure and logistics, with a focus on screening procedures and equipment operators. He said this would boost tourist arrivals, particularly along Sabah's east coast, which was overseen by the Eastern Sabah Security Command.

items.title: Karoline Leavitt to step down as Trump's press secretary
items.summary: WASHINGTON: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who earned a reputation for acid putdowns of journalists, is to step down, President Donald Trump announced Wednesday adding she would remain a senior advisor. Leavitt, 28, the youngest ever US presidential top spokesperson, has been a fiercely loyal Trump defender, delivering fluent and aggressive performances at often combative press briefings. "Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family," Trump said on social media.

items.title: Milky Mist's US$163m IPO fully subscribed
items.summary: The company raised 4.65 billion rupees from 19 anchor investors, including Singapore state investor Temasek, the International Finance Corporation and HDFC Mutual Fund, ahead of the IPO. The 15.53 billion rupees (US$162.96 million) IPO comprises a fresh issue worth 14.28 billion rupees and an offer for sale worth 1.25 billion rupees by founders Sathishkumar T and Anitha S. The company cut the IPO size from 20.35 billion rupees after pre-listing deals with Temasek's Jongsong Investments, which acquired a roughly 5.2 per cent stake in the company. Milky Mist's profit rose about 176 per cent to 1.27 billion rupees in the year ended March 31.

items.title: Rob Reiner son denies grand jury murder charges
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: The son of legendary US film director Rob Reiner denied new charges of killing both his parents when he appeared in court on Wednesday after grand jury indictments were unsealed. Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder, with the special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and murder by means of lying in wait. Rob Reiner, the son of legendary comedian Carl Reiner, started his showbiz career in acting.

items.title: Global youth unemployment at 12.4pc in 2025, says ILO
items.summary: GLOBAL youth unemployment increased last year as weaker economic growth, geopolitical tensions and sluggish job creation made it harder for young people to find work, said the International Labour Organisation (ILO) yesterday. The global unemployment rate among 15- to 24-year-olds rose to 12.4 per cent last year from 12.3 per cent in 2023, equivalent to 67 million people, according to a new report by the United Nations labour agency. The ILO said the share of young people not in employment, education or training also edged higher to 20 per cent, representing more than 257 million people.

items.title: UK 'joke' candidate Binface pushes serious point about politics
items.summary: But in a pantheon of colourful characters, Count Binface, a man wearing a rubbish bin over his head, is stealing the show. The self-described "intergalactic space warrior" from the fictional planet Sigma IX takes on hardline anti-immigrant politician Nigel Farage on Thursday in the Clacton by-election, triggered when the Reform UK leader resigned in a shock move. During almost a decade as the joke candidate in UK politics, Binface has fully embraced the absurd.

items.title: Tourists rush to Mount Etna as Italian volcano erupts
items.summary: ROME: Spectacular images of lava flowing down the slopes of an erupting Mount Etna have drawn flocks of tourists to the Italian volcano – to the worry of local guides. The tallest active volcano in Europe, Etna has been spewing ash and lava for days, forcing the closure of the nearby Catania airport, a key gateway for tourists visiting the island of Sicily. "They all want to come and see the lava flow, everyone is drawn to this unique beauty," Daniele Perricelli, 41, a local guide told AFP on Wednesday.

items.title: Trump says US will 'keep' Hormuz strait control
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the United States is in control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz and will "keep it." "The U.S.A. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. Late Tuesday, Trump told reporters: "We have total control over the Hormuz Strait right now.

items.title: Zhu Rongji, trailblazing ex-premier who transformed China's economy
items.summary: ZHU Rongji, China's former premier who died on Wednesday aged 97, championed free-market policies and delivered far-reaching economic reforms during his five years at the helm. Rumoured to be descended from Zhu Yuanzhang, the founding emperor of the Ming dynasty, Zhu was born in the central city of Changsha in 1928 into a China riven by civil war. Zhu studied electrical engineering at Beijing's elite Tsinghua University and joined the Communist Party in 1949, the same year leader Mao Zedong declared the creation of the "New China."

items.title: 15-year-old boy drowns while swimming in river
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 15-year-old boy drowned while swimming with friends in a river near Masjid Ulu Pulai, Kampung Ulu Pulai, Gelang Patah, yesterday. Pekan Nanas Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Md Bakhtiar Chik said the department received an emergency call at 6.15pm. He said 17 firefighters, assisted by four fire engines, were deployed to the scene, about 15km away.

items.title: Soldier injured by fellow serviceman's shot at Port Dickson firing range
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A soldier was injured after he was believed to have been hit by a shot fired by a fellow serviceman at a firing range in Sungai Menyala, Port Dickson, yesterday. Negri Sembilan deputy police chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Nasharudin Mohd Shariff said police received a report on the incident, which occurred at 2.15pm. He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was at the firing range with several other personnel when he was believed to have been hit by a shot fired by a fellow serviceman.

items.title: French buyers rethinking housing choices after heatwaves
items.summary: AFTER multiple severe heatwaves in a single summer, French residents are increasingly factoring high temperatures into their home hunts, realtors say, bumping up features such as shutters, air conditioning and indirect sunlight on their priority lists. "On the top floor of a Haussmann-style building, the heat indoors can become truly unbearable," said Joseph Denke, an estate agent with FredeLion in Paris. "We're seeing that heatwaves are happening in June or even May," the 30-year-old said.

items.title: Taliban govt building diplomacy despite lack of recognition
items.summary: FIVE years after returning to power, Afghanistan's Taliban authorities have built working relationships with a slate of countries, despite a lack of formal recognition. Russia remains the only nation to officially recognise the Taliban government. But many states are nevertheless engaging with Afghanistan's leaders, including Britain and European Union members, driven largely by practical considerations.

items.title: NST Leader: 5 BNM warnings, yet no action by Tabung Haji
items.summary: THE revelation that Bank Negara Malaysia issued five warnings to Tabung Haji between 2014 and 2017 over its financial position raises a fundamental question: How was the warning from the country's central bank allowed to be repeatedly ignored? Five warnings cannot be dismissed as oversight. Tabung Haji, being a statutory body, is governed by the Tabung Haji Act 1995, meaning the board's statutory powers, duties and governance are regulated by the act.

items.title: 447 red-tape reform projects generate RM2.95bil in compliance savings
items.summary: He said another 500 RKB projects were planned for next year, with the government targeting RM2.5 billion in savings. Shamsul Azri said the RKB framework was part of the government's wider public service reform efforts to improve efficiency. Shamsul Azri said Malaysia's government efficiency ranking improved from 25th to 14th, while business efficiency rose from 32nd to 16th.

items.title: Colombia declares three days mourning for quake victims
items.summary: BOGOTA: Colombia on Wednesday declared three days of mourning for victims of an earthquake that demolished buildings in the west of the country, killing more than 200 people. In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures. Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

items.title: Cops hunt loan shark over paint attacks on dead man's family
items.summary: Sungai Buloh district police chief Superintendent Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police received a report on Aug 6 after the complainant discovered the damage. He said the incident was believed to have occurred at 7.50am on Aug 5. "The notice contained a claim regarding a loan debt involving the complainant's late son," he said in a statement.

items.title: Uncle, 8-year-old nephew die in Klang shoplot blaze
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Two people died while two others were rescued after a fire broke out at a three-storey shoplot in Taman Bayu Perdana, Klang, this evening. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.51pm before personnel from the Port Klang Fire and Rescue Station arrived eight minutes later. "After the fire was extinguished, two other victims who were trapped were found in separate toilets at 6.33pm," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report to go to police, MACC, Bank Negara, IRB for full investigation, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will go to the relevant authorities for a full investigation based on all findings and information contained in the report, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. “This includes information contained in the report, as well as additional information provided by Finance Minister II (Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan) and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Tabung Haji RCI report, yesterday.” The TH RCI report was made public on July 29.

items.title: Two accused flee Kulim court, one slides down pillar to escape police
items.summary: KULIM, Aug 12 — Two men attending a case mention at the Kulim Magistrate’s Court here today fled the court compound after spotting police officers waiting to re-arrest them in connection with another case. Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the incident occurred at about 10am after both accused, aged 27 and 31, had completed their case mention and document submission. The case was fixed for re-mention on June 8, July 12 and today for document submission and case management,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Rubbish lorry crashes through Pantai Hillpark condo wall, crushes three cars
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — A rubbish lorry believed to have suffered brake failure lost control and crashed into a condominium boundary wall, crushing three cars at Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the lorry was travelling downhill along a straight, sloping road when the incident occurred at about 4.10am. The lorry driver, a 41-year-old local man, suffered an injury to his left leg, he said.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Prices of non subsidised RON97, RON95, diesel cheaper by 20, 15 and 10 sen respectively from Aug 13 to 19
items.summary: According to a statement by the Ministry of Finance (MoF), for the stated period, the price of RON97 is set at RM4.15 per litre compared to RM4.35 previously, while unsubsidised RON95 is priced at RM3.62 per litre compared to RM3.77, and unsubsidised diesel is set at RM4.47 per litre compared to RM4.57 previously. At the same time, subsidised petroleum prices remain unchanged at RM1.99 per litre for RON95 under Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) and RM2.10 per litre for diesel under Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel). Prices for the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control Systems (SKDS) remain at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre , respectively.

items.title: Singapore fugitive flees to Johor, ends up kidnapped for S$80,000 ransom
items.summary: Federal Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the victim, who is wanted by the Singapore police, had initially entered the country illegally at the end of May. He said the victim was met by one of the six suspects in Johor Bahru shortly before his 28-year-old girlfriend also entered the country illegally. “The suspects also forcefully took the victim’s cash consisting of S$12,000 and RM41,400.

items.title: Five Chinese nationals arrested in Sri Petaling, Pudu over housebreakings in KL
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said investigations revealed that the suspects may have been involved in a housebreaking incident in Taman Desa Petaling on August 4, which caused the victim to suffer losses of about RM6,000 involving cash, jewelry, and a luxury-branded sling bag. “During the raid at approximately 9.30pm, the police also seized a vehicle along with various tools used for housebreaking,” he said in a statement today. Fadil said the police also recovered items belonging to the victim alongside various other luxury items including watches, wallets, and cash in various foreign currencies totalling more than RM10,000.

items.title: Kedah woman pleads guilty to organising RM1.7m kootu fund scheme
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 12 — A woman pleaded guilty at the Sessions Court here today to organising a kootu fund scheme, resulting in estimated losses of more than RM1.7 million between July last year and July this year. Siti Zulaika Ahmad Sabri, 36, entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Sharmila Abdul Samad. According to the charge, Siti Zulaika allegedly organised a kootu fund involving 52 participants aged between 24 and 62, with each participant required to contribute cash to the scheme in Kampung Padang Satu, Bukit Kayu Hitam, Changlun.

items.title: Kelantan state assembly passes Syariah Criminal Offences Bill 2026
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Kelantan state legislative assembly today passed the Syariah Criminal Offences (Kelantan) Bill 2026 to streamline and strengthen its provisions, making them more systematic, clear and authoritative. The winding-up speech was delivered by Mohamed Fadzli and Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud before the Bill was read for the second and third time and subsequently passed unanimously in the presence of Kelantan state assembly Speaker Datuk Mohd Amar Nik Abdullah. Earlier, Mohd Nassuruddin said the Bill was not drafted without careful planning.

items.title: Sarawak closes 108 schools in Serian division as API readings exceed 200
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 12 — A total of 108 schools in the Serian Division have been temporarily closed after Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the area exceeded 200, reaching the very unhealthy range. Uggah said air quality in Sarawak had shown an upward trend in API readings since Aug 1. Uggah said SDMC and relevant agencies would continue monitoring air quality, weather conditions, hotspots and fire incidents throughout the state.

items.title: KLIA CCTV monitoring to be improved to address blind spots, says home minister
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) will improve the closed-circuit television (CCTV) system at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) if there are blind spots. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said there are currently 5,000 CCTVs at KLIA Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, but the monitoring aspect of the system also needs attention. “Just equipment, infra.

items.title: Anwar thanks Brunei Sultan for prayers, concern after surgery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today received a phone call from Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei Darussalam, who enquired about his health and prayed for his well-being. In a Facebook post, Anwar expressed his appreciation for the Sultan’s prayers and concern. Anwar also said he would have an audience with Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah in Bandar Seri Begawan next week in conjunction with the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC) between Malaysia and Brunei.

items.title: Malaysia, Thailand step up cooperation on border security, cross-border crime
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Thailand are strengthening border security cooperation through government-to-government (G2G) and police-to-police (P2P) platforms, including addressing cross-border crime threats. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that the G2G cooperation is implemented through the Malaysia-Thailand Border Security Management Committee, which meets twice a year. He said that the P2P cooperation involves the states bordering Thailand, namely Perlis, Kedah and Kelantan, to ensure that security aspects are always given attention.

items.title: IPTS student charged with murder after alleged drunk-driving incident in Kuala Langat
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — A student of a private higher education institution (IPTS) who went viral after allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol was charged in the Telok Datok Magistrates’ Court in Kuala Langat today with murdering an elderly man last week. According to the charge, the man is accused of murdering Eng Kim Kheng @ Ng Kim Swee, 78, at Kilometre 38, Jalan Klang-Banting-Port Dickson, in the Kuala Langat district at about 7.20pm on August 7. Previously, a video recording of an accident at the Kanchong Bengkok traffic light intersection in Banting went viral, showing a man admitting to driving under the influence of alcohol while another man was seen lying on the road with a leg injury.

items.title: Fresh RCI into Tabung Haji’s 2021-2025 performance needs Agong’s consent, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Any decision to form a fresh Royal Commission of Inquiry to scrutinise Lembaga Tabung Haji’s performance from 2021 to 2025 will need the Agong’s consent first, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. The Anwar government tabled the report of the inquiry’s findings in a special Parliamentary sitting for debate yesterday, more than three years after the report was published. TH lost billions from poor investments, the inquiry found, prompting the authorities to crack down on those named in the report.

items.title: Fadhlina: Character education is more than teaching youths to be ‘good’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Character education should encourage young people to voice their views, think critically and remain respectful when faced with differing opinions, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said. In a Facebook post today, Fadhlina said that at the National Madani Youth Forum, she observed young people learning to articulate their thoughts, express their positions, consider differing views and defend their arguments. We want them to speak up confidently, think critically and remain respectful when opinions differ,” she said.

items.title: Socso incentive claims land four Melaka company directors in court
items.summary: The company directors were accused of providing two Perkeso agents with documents, namely the Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Verification Form under the company's name containing false information, attached in an incentive claim application under the Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Programme. The first accused, Henry Ratnaike, 45, who is the Director of Alpha Buildcon, faces four charges of committing the offence at Taman Merdeka Jaya, Batu Berendam, in the district of Melaka Tengah on May 10, 2024. All three accused were charged with committing offences under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act.

items.title: Got haze health worries? Ministry steps up monitoring, medical readiness
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Health Ministry (MOH) is strengthening surveillance of haze-related illnesses at health facilities following 10 stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with nine in Sarawak and one in Selangor. Educational institutions, government agencies and the private sector were also advised to monitor API readings and adjust outdoor activities according to the air quality level. MOH also reminded the public not to carry out open burning, which could worsen air quality and increase health risks caused by haze.

items.title: Immigration blames airline systems for long-validity passport headaches
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Difficulties experienced by holders of Malaysian International Passports (PMA) with validity periods exceeding 10 years while travelling abroad were caused by systems used by certain airlines, rather than the immigration control systems of foreign countries, according to the Immigration Department. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said that, in terms of border controls and International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards, passports with validity periods exceeding 10 years did not pose a problem. Zakaria said the issue involved, among other things, systems used by airlines that set the maximum passport validity period at 10 years.

items.title: Haze worsens in Malaysia as 11 stations record unhealthy API, Serian reaches 204
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Malaysia has been experiencing haze since August 8, with 11 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and one station in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy reading as of 3pm today, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) said. In a statement today, the ministry said the El Niño phenomenon occurring alongside the Southwest Monsoon had resulted in several areas, particularly southern Peninsular Malaysia and western and southern Sarawak, receiving below-average rainfall. As of 3pm today, 11 of the 68 air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy API readings.

items.title: Airport security plan heads to Cabinet next week after Malaysian pilot’s drug bust
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — A plan to enhance airport security controls will be presented to the Cabinet next week following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia on suspicion of drug smuggling, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the matter was discussed at last week’s Cabinet meeting, which instructed all relevant regulatory agencies to draw up plans to strengthen airport security. The agencies included the Home Ministry, Transport Ministry, Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Aviation Security, Malaysia Aviation Commission (MAVCOM) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), he said.

items.title: Malaysia, Saudi Arabia sign pact to share judicial know-how
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Saudi Arabia today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in the judicial field. The MoU was signed by Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia Azhaniz Teh Azman Teh and Saudi Arabian Minister of Justice Sheikh Dr Waleed Mohammed Alsmani at the Palace of Justice here. The MoU signing, witnessed by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, was held in conjunction with Sheikh Dr Waleed’s official visit to Malaysia.

items.title: Property crime pushes Pahang crime index higher in first seven months of 2026
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 12 — The Pahang crime index increased by 105 cases to 1,262 cases from January to July this year, compared to 1,157 cases for the same period last year. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the rate of resolving crime cases decreased to 59.58 per cent from 71.74 per cent. Azry Akmar said that although the number of commercial cases increased, the recorded loss value decreased 9.8 per cent to RM46.3 million, compared to RM51.3 million last year.

items.title: Kedah PAS vows to continue fight against gambling after Federal Court ruling
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 12 — Kedah PAS today vowed to continue its efforts to eliminate gambling in the state despite the Federal Court dismissing the state government’s bid to appeal a ruling against its ban on issuing and renewing gambling premises licences. Kedah PAS commissioner Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party accepted the court’s decision but expressed disappointment over the outcome. “Kedah Pas takes note of the Federal Court’s decision to reject the Kedah government’s application for leave to appeal over the cessation of gambling premises licences.

items.title: Worried govt producing GMO rice? Agriculture Ministry says Perak run is only a controlled test
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 12 — The proposed genetically modified rice field trial in Perak involving the MR219 variety is only a controlled test plot and does not constitute approval for the use of genetically modified organism (GMO) crops in Malaysia, said Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak. He said the trial was intended to generate scientific evidence and data on GMO, particularly its potential role in addressing food security challenges, rather than to allow its commercial use. Isham assured that the test plot would be conducted under controlled, monitored and documented conditions to ensure that any potential issues would not spread beyond the trial area.

items.title: RM200,000-plus aid for family of cop killed in Sabah electric shock incident, says home minister
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will expedite benefits and welfare assistance for the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, who died in an electric shock incident in Beaufort, Sabah, last Thursday. He said today’s visit to the late officer’s family home, accompanied by Bukit Aman Management director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and Sabah deputy police commissioner Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin, was also a gesture of sympathy from the entire police force. Saifuddin Nasution said the assistance presented included contributions from the Sabah and Kelantan Police Contingents (IPK), as well as takaful payments from the deceased’s contributions as a member of the Police Cooperative, with total contributions and payments exceeding RM200,000.

items.title: Court of Appeal says Malaysia is not the right forum for 1MDB suit against UK law firm White & Case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Court of Appeal today granted an appeal by UK law firm White & Case LLP against a High Court ruling that allowed a lawsuit filed by 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) on alleged fraud to be heard in Malaysia. In a unanimous decision, a three-judge panel chaired by Justice Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, sitting with Justices K. Muniandy and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, ruled that the Kuala Lumpur High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm. The court ordered 1MDB to pay RM130,000 in costs to White & Case.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt raises RM48m in sponsorships for Merdeka, Malaysia Day celebrations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Sponsorships for this year’s Merdeka and Malaysia Day celebrations have risen to more than RM48 million, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil announced today, describing the contributions as a “public-private partnership” success. Of the total, RM2.7 million was contributed in cash, while the remaining RM45.93 million comprised contributions in the form of goods and services. “The ministry is deeply honoured to announce that the total value of sponsorship for HKHM 2026, as verified by the Ministry of Communications Sponsorship Committee to date, amounts to RM48.63 million,” the minister said at an event to celebrate the sponsors here.

items.title: Perak DAP says it will remain in unity govt, back Anwar’s reform agenda
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 12 — Perak DAP has unanimously decided to remain in the Unity Government and mobilise the party’s entire machinery to fulfil the people’s mandate and continue the country’s reform agenda. In a statement today, Perak DAP said the decision was made to deliver on its election promises under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “DAP must continue to demonstrate its capabilities through achievements and work performance so as not to disappoint the people’s expectations.

items.title: Ipoh married couple charged with trafficking 480.6g MDMA, face death penalty
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 12 — A married couple was charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with trafficking 480.6 grammes of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) last week. According to the charge, they were jointly accused of trafficking 480.6 grammes of MDMA at Room M333, The Pearl Orient Sdn Bhd, Bercham Bistari 4, Medan Bercham Bistari, in the Kinta district, at about 10.30 pm on Aug 4. During the raids, police seized ketamine and MDMA, including about 2.6 kilogrammes of MDMA found at two houses in Tapah.
